## Intent
Hypothesis: delegating integrate+decide to an AOT-compiled Halide kernel producing a 1 B/p mask intermediate can approach the streaming ceiling by vectorizing math+decide, with the mask enabling a cheap host-side respawn scan.

## Layout & approach
The 69 B/p AoS layout offers 28 hot bytes (41%) for loops 1 and 3, but only 4 hot bytes (5%) for loop 2 — the rest is dead weight per line. The 1 B/p mask intermediate stays cache-resident into DRAM. Loop 1 delegates to `_halide_b6_mask` (external AOT); loop 2 is a branchy host-side mask scan; loop 3 is scalar render with byte-granular color writes. At 41% hot, effective bandwidth caps at ~41% of raw transfers for loops 1/3, ~5% for loop 2. Spills: L1d at N≈949, L2 at N≈60787.

## Cache saturation
At q=0.01, ns/p is flat across regimes: ~6.5–6.9 in L1d/L2, dropping to ~6.0–6.1 in DRAM (N≥62000). No spill knee — the algo is compute/overhead-bound, so larger N amortizes fixed Halide setup. L1d→L2 at N≈949 is invisible (6.56→6.65 ns/p); L2→DRAM at N≈60787 actually improves cost (6.23→6.06) because 41% hot means cache residency adds little when scalar compute dominates. No hidden knee at any death rate.

## Bandwidth
Peak BW is 11.48 GB/s (q=0.01, N=150000) — 38% of the 29.9 GB/s ceiling, 2.6x the 2.308 ns/p floor. Compute-bound at low q (66–80% compute); transitions to branch- and backend-bound at high q — at q=0.5, N=1M, branch_flush hits 20.7% and BW drops to 6.37 GB/s (21% of ceiling); at q=0.25, N=100000, backend_stall reaches 66.6%. Vs baseline: 0.71–0.90x (faster) everywhere, improving at higher q. Vs winner: 1.35–2.03x slower everywhere.

## Assembly
Entirely scalar: 0 vector instructions across 532 insns. Loop 1 calls `_halide_b6_mask` via `bl` after a `stp` buffer-setup prologue — the kernel may vectorize internally but the host pays call overhead per frame. Respawn is unrolled 32x: `ldp q1, q0` + `orr.16b` + `ext.16b` for bulk zero-check, then 32 `ldrb`+`cbz`+`bl _spawn` chains. Render uses scalar `fadd`/`fmul`/`fsub`/`fcvtzs` with `csel` clamping and `strb` byte stores. The 91 cond-branches per iteration and 16 byte-scatters explain the 38% ceiling cap.

## Verdict
Partially refuted — beats naive scalar everywhere (0.71–0.90x baseline, 1.1–1.4x faster) but never approaches the ceiling (38% at best, 2.6x the floor) and never beats the winner (1.35–2.03x slower). The host step is entirely scalar (0 vector insns), the Halide call adds per-frame overhead, and the 32x-unrolled branchy respawn with per-byte `cbz`+`bl _spawn` dominates at high q (branch_flush 20.7% at q=0.5, N=1M). The compact mask is sound but the call-delegated architecture and scalar `strb` render prevent streaming.
